title: Advocates Act s. 24 — Persons who may be admitted as advocates on a State roll (Advocates Act s. 24)

content.overview: Section 24 allows admission of a citizen of India, aged at least twenty-one, who holds a law degree from a recognised university and meets the other enacted conditions. Reciprocity can qualify a foreign national as the section provides. The Council admits. The degree does not.

cases.name: Bar Council of Maharashtra v. M.V. Dabholkar
cases.facts: The Court considered disciplinary control over conduct affecting the legal profession.
cases.issue: What is the public purpose of professional discipline?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Disciplinary jurisdiction protects the integrity of the profession and the administration of justice, not merely private client interests.
cases.holding: The Court affirmed the public character of professional discipline.
cases.relevance: Use for the object and standing of disciplinary proceedings.

cases.name: Ex-Capt. Harish Uppal v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court considered advocates' strikes and court boycotts.
cases.issue: Whether advocates have a right to strike or abstain from court work.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Advocates have no right to strike or call for a boycott that obstructs administration of justice.
cases.holding: The Court directed that courts should not routinely adjourn matters because of strikes.
cases.relevance: Use for duties to court and professional responsibility.

cases.name: Supreme Court Bar Association v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court examined the relationship between contempt jurisdiction and professional disciplinary power.
cases.issue: Can a contempt court suspend an advocate's licence to practise?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The power to discipline an advocate professionally belongs to the statutory Bar Council structure, while the court retains contempt jurisdiction within its constitutional and statutory limits.
cases.holding: The Court separated contempt punishment from professional suspension powers.
cases.relevance: Use to distinguish contempt from disciplinary proceedings.
